title: 3: Private Apartments
html:
3: Private Apartments

Residents and long-term visitors rent apartments in this tenement building. The complex's most notable resident is also its landlord, a crotchety jeweler who invests in gemstones and other valuables.

When the characters arrive at the apartments, read the following boxed text aloud:

A wooden jeweler's sign hangs over an open door in the front of this two-story building. Inside, an old human man hunches over a table, peering at an emerald through a jeweler's loupe.

The jeweler, Lenk, puts down his loupe with a sigh and invites the characters in.

Lenk

Human Jeweler

  • Statblock:. Noble

This elderly jeweler can identify and appraise any gemstone.

  • Faultfinder. Lenk has a knack for spotting flaws, be they in things or people.
  • Pessimistic. Lenk always sees the worst part of any situation.
  • "Your money isn't safe at the bank. I hear a burglar broke in recently and stole every last coin." (Partially true; the burglar was unsuccessful)
  • "Some stones hide things. The next time you're in an ancient dungeon or old cave, inspect the walls closely. You just might find a secret door." (True)

Apartments Features

The apartments have the following features:

  • Apartments. Each two-story apartment is a section of the same large tenement building. The apartments have identical amenities: a stove, a small drawing room, a bedroom, and a storage area.
  • Rain Barrel. A large barrel near the building holds clean water for washing dishes and clothes.

Apartments Services

The apartments offer the following services:

  • Buy Gems. Lenk can buy gems the characters find in their adventures. Lenk exchanges gems at this location for their value in gold. All the gems in this adventure are worth 100 GP; this rate includes Lenk's appraisal fee.
  • Rent an Apartment. Characters can rent an apartment for 100 GP per month.

Quest: Breaking the Bank

After detailing the services he offers, Lenk tells the characters he's exploring a new line of business. Read the following boxed text aloud:

"With reports of bandits along the trail and the occasional thief here in the keep, I plan to sell strongboxes to help citizens and travelers secure their valuables. I've received a few samples made by local crafters who hope to partner with me in this new venture, but I won't stake my reputation on shoddy handiwork.

"I need to determine which of the strongboxes are fit for sale, and you look like a capable lot. Care to test your mettle on some metal?"

If the characters agree, Lenk hands each of them a locked iron strongbox and instructs them to try to pilfer its contents however they please. Each strongbox contains a modest amount of gold. If a character can get into a strongbox, they can keep its contents, though Lenk doesn't reveal what's inside.

Cracking the Strongboxes

A character can make one attempt to open a strongbox through any of the following means:

  • Breaking the Strongbox. Each strongbox is a Tiny object with AC 19, 5 HP, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability to Cold damage. A character who reduces a strongbox to 0 Hit Points with a single attack or spell destroys the strongbox but not its contents.

Picking the Lock (A character who has Thieves' Tools). A character that can use Thieves' Tools to pick the strongbox's lock, doing so with a successful 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.

  • Prying Open the Lid. A character can force open a strongbox's lid with a successful 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

At the DM's discretion, other methods of opening a strongbox might exist.

Reward

Inside each strongbox is 5 GP. If the characters manage to penetrate all the strongboxes, Lenk grouses about the boxes' poor craftsmanship. If all the strongboxes thwart their attempts, Lenk pays each character 1 GP as a consolation and says there are nobler skills to master than thievery.

This elderly jeweler can identify and appraise any gemstone.

  • Faultfinder. Lenk has a knack for spotting flaws, be they in things or people.

title: 4: Smithy
html:
4: Smithy

The smithy is where the keep's residents purchase metal goods and have them repaired.

When the characters arrive at the smithy, read the following boxed text aloud:

The stench of hot smoke and the sound of clanging metal fill this smithy. Lit by the orange glow of a forge, a dark-haired dwarf pounds a molten ingot at an anvil behind a low wooden counter. Sparks fly with every strike of her hammer.

The hard-working smith is Kalista.

Kalista

Dwarf Blacksmith

  • Statblock:. Commoner

The keep's taciturn, hardworking smith prefers to let her hammer do the talking.

  • Standoffish. Kalista is curt toward people she doesn't know, especially adventurers.
  • Stern. Kalista never cracks a smile.
  • "Every now and then, adventurers return from the Caves of Chaos with magic weapons, but most of the time they don't come back at all." (True)
  • "Mind your equipment around oozes. Their touch can corrode even the sturdiest of metals." (True)

Smithy Features

The smithy has the following features:

  • Forge. The large forge behind the counter fills most of the smithy's lower floor. Water barrels and bellows flank the forge.
  • Mundane Goods. A few stout posts support the upper floor. They bear hanging tools and everyday metal goods: cast-iron pots, horseshoes, and so on.
  • Private Rooms. Two doors at the rear of the smithy lead to storerooms containing ingots and spare tools. A third door opens to a washbasin and spiral stairs that ascend to Kalista's quarters.
A Blacksmith's Hammer and Anvil

Smithy Services

The smithy offers the following service:

  • Leather Branding. For 1 GP, Kalista can brand anything made of leather, such as Leather Armor or a Spellbook, with the keep's coat of arms.

Kalista makes armaments but doesn't sell them. She forges them exclusively for the keep's armed forces.

Quest: Tools of Destruction

If a character asks to purchase armor or weapons, Kalista explains why she no longer sells those to outsiders. Read the following boxed text aloud:

"I used to sell arms and armor to would-be heroes like you. I had heard reports of foolhardy adventurers falling victim to brigands and monsters. I shrugged those stories off for a time.

"Last winter, the castellan's forces thwarted an assault on the keep. After the onslaught, I was sickened to learn that many of the attackers' weapons bore my maker's mark. By selling to outsiders, I had unwittingly armed our enemies. I vowed then never to forge another weapon for anyone but the keep's soldiers. I haven't since."

The keep's soldiers occasionally bring confiscated weapons to Kalista for destruction.

Weapon Smelting

Kalista recently received a cartload of battered and rusted weapons seized by the keep's defenders. She asks the characters to help melt them down.

The disarmament process takes 1 hour. To aid Kalista with it, the characters must succeed on the following ability checks in this order:

13 Strength (Athletics). The character piles the weapons in the forge and undertakes the tough labor needed to properly melt them down.

13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). The character carefully tips a crucible of molten metal into an ingot mold without spillage.

If at least one character succeeds on each check, the party completes the disarmament. The characters can retry failed checks, but if they accumulate three failures, Kalista dismisses them with a sigh, insisting she can handle the rest of the job herself.

If the characters successfully help Kalista destroy the weapons, she pays them each 5 GP.

title: 5: Provisioner's Shop
html:
5: Provisioner's Shop

This cluttered shop provides supplies for travelers who venture into the wilderness.

When the characters arrive at the shop, read the following boxed text aloud:

Dusty rays of sunlight stream into this general store through small windows near the ceiling. Barrels, bottles, boxes, and other supplies crowd its shelves.

An affable halfling named Ruckus runs this shop.

Ruckus

Halfling Shopkeeper

  • Statblock:. Commoner

The owner of the provisioner's shop is small but has a big personality.

  • Loud. Ruckus compensates for his short stature by shouting up to taller customers.
  • Everything Has a Place. Despite the mess in his shop, Ruckus always knows exactly where to find just what he's looking for.
  • "I hear goblins throw wild parties." (Oh Yeah!)
  • "Lenk the jeweler gives a fair price for gems and precious stones. He lives in the private apartments." (True)

Shop Features

The shop has the following features:

  • Brimming with Supplies. Everyday supplies fill the shop's packed interior. Shelves, crates, chests, and cabinets overflow with clothes, blankets, tools, trinkets, toys, and other miscellaneous junk.
  • Private Rooms. A side entrance leads to a few low rooms where Ruckus lives.
  • Storage. A storeroom door toward the back of the shop is roped off and bears a hastily scrawled sign that reads, "WARNING! FIRE GHOST. STAY OUT!" Inside the storeroom, jumbled goods cram floor-to-ceiling shelves.

Shop Services

The Provisioner Handout lists items available for sale. Give this handout to the players whenever they visit this location. Ruckus might point proudly at some of the illustrations to invite comment about how nice they look.

Items for Sale
ItemCost
Acid25 GP
Antitoxin50 GP
Ball Bearings1 GP
Potion of Healing50 GP
Healer's Kit5 GP
Hooded Lantern5 GP
Rope1 GP
Musical Instruments for Sale
InstrumentCost
Drum6 GP
Flute2 GP
Lute35 GP
Viol30 GP
Provisioner Handout

Quest: Fire Ghost

If the characters don't bring up the unusual sign on the storeroom door, Ruckus soon mentions it and asks for their help in resolving the matter. Read the following boxed text aloud:

"I've been smelling smoke in the storeroom for the past few days. Yesterday I peeked inside and saw a cloaked figure smoldering like an ember—surely it was a fire ghost! I threw a flagon of ale at it to put out the fire, but I haven't dared to enter the room since. Someone braver than me should lay the ghost to rest. Maybe you could do it?"

The "Ghost"

The only thing haunting the shopkeeper is his own reckless disorganization. Ruckus recently relocated some inventory to a shelf in his storeroom; the merchandise included a hefty magnifying glass. On sunny days, the light through a high window focuses through the lens on a dusty old cloak, causing it to smolder. It's a major fire hazard.

Ruckus's decision to leave the storeroom alone compounds the danger. If the problem isn't dealt with soon, a conflagration is inevitable.

Investigating the Scene

Characters can get at the truth by investigating the jumbled storeroom, where they discover a singed cloak stained with dried ale.

Gathering Clues

Characters in the storeroom can gather clues by succeeding on one of the following ability checks. Consider these examples:

13 Intelligence (Nature). At noon each day, sunlight from the window shines on the cloak.

12 Wisdom (Perception). High on a shelf near the storeroom window, a magnifying glass protrudes from an open box.

Storeroom Box

Solving the Case

After inspecting the storeroom, the characters can draw their conclusions. A character who considers the evidence and succeeds on a 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check correctly deduces the source of the smoke and the risk it poses to Ruckus's shop. A character who gathered one or both clues has Advantage on this check.

If the characters explain the situation, Ruckus is relieved to hear his shop isn't haunted and corrects the fire hazard. As thanks, he pays each character 10 GP and encourages them to spend it here.

title: 6: Trader's Shop
html:
6: Trader's Shop

Only bold traders bring goods to the Borderlands.

When the characters arrive at the shop, read the following boxed text aloud:

Awnings extend over weapon racks and armor stands at this trader's shop. Inside, a tall human woman polishes a suit of armor with an oily rag.

The woman is Oleira, the shop's owner. The trader's shop is a family business. She runs it with her two teenage sons, Derlo and Ulmar, who dream of being brave knights rather than shopkeepers.

Oleira

Human Shopkeeper

  • Statblock:. Commoner

This merchant and mother of two deals in wares ranging from common trade goods to curious bric-a-brac.

  • Fastidious. Oleira can't stand dusty wares. Every item must be spotless.
  • Parental. Oleira sometimes treats her customers like she does her children.
  • "A hermit, Xanthe, was cast out of the keep for practicing evil magic. I hear she was in a cult. Think of the children!" (False)
  • "The keep's two outer gate guards, Bartho and Gala, are both so green. I'm not sure which of them I trust less to protect us." (True)

Shop Features

The trader's shop has the following features:

  • Indoor Display. The shop interior contains minor luxuries such as salt, spices, cloth, and furniture, which Oleira sells only to citizens of the keep. The goods are clean and well organized.
  • Outdoor Display. When the shop is open, Oleira displays armor and weapons under the awning.
  • Warehouse. Behind the shop is a small warehouse, where Oleira receives, sorts, and stores goods.
A suit of armor for sale

Shop Services

The Trader Handout lists items available for sale. Give this handout to the players whenever they visit this location.

Sturdy Armors and Shields
ArmorCost
Breastplate400 GP
Splint Armor200 GP
Shield10 GP
Studded Leather Armor45 GP
Useful Weapons
WeaponCost
Maul10 GP
Rapier25 GP
Longsword15 GP
Spear1 GP
Trader Handout

Quest: Dangerous Stowaway

As the characters browse Oleira's wares, she offers them each 1 GP to unload a wagon while her sons are off watching soldiers train elsewhere in the keep. The delivery is late, so Oleira tells the characters to meet the wagon along the trail.

Unknown to Oleira, the shipment contains a dangerous stowaway. During transit, a nasty ooze slithered onto the wagon and gobbled up its driver. Oozes usually lurk in dark places like caves or dungeons, but they go wherever they can sate their voracious appetites.

Ooze Surprise

If the characters agree, the guards at the outer gate nod at them as they exit the keep and head down the trail. When the characters come across the wagon, read the following boxed text aloud:

You find the wagon standing in the middle of the trail with no driver in sight. Some of the crates in the wagon glisten wetly.

A Gray Ooze Glob lurks within the abandoned wagon, waiting to ambush the characters. When the characters approach the wagon, the ooze seeps from the supplies with a hideous squelching noise and fights the characters. Roll Initiative!

Preparing for Combat

Use the "Combat" section of the D&D Beyond Basic Rules, along with the Trail Map and the Gray Ooze Glob stat block, to run this encounter.

Reward

After defeating the ooze, carting the goods is straightforward work. When the characters return to Oleira, she's shocked to learn of the ooze—she or her sons could've been seriously harmed.

To show her gratitude, Oleira exceeds her original offer, paying each character 5 GP for their heroism.

title: 7: Bank
html:
7: Bank

The keep's residents and visitors store their most valuable belongings and savings in the bank.

When the characters arrive at the bank, read the following boxed text aloud:

This one-story bank sports a teller's window with a drop-down counter. A bespectacled halfling woman in a silk tabard sits behind the glass. Outside, a bored human guard stands watch.

The banker, Quink, relies on the keep's soldiers for protection. Yvette is stationed here most days to discourage anyone from hassling Quink.

Quink

Halfling Banker

  • Statblock:. Noble

Quink is a miserly moneylender.

  • Frugal. Quink never budges on matters of money.
  • Garrulous. Conversations with Quink last twice as long as they should.
  • "Good supplies are a sound investment. Ruckus at the provisioner's shop can outfit you with quality gear." (True)
  • "I've heard dragons are a bit like bankers—we obsess over every coin. If you ever encounter a dragon, don't touch its hoard unless you want to meet its wrath." (True)

Yvette

Human Bank Guard

  • Statblock:. Guard

This corrupt guard exploits her station for selfish ends.

  • Bitter. Yvette thinks the world owes her.
  • Grifter. Yvette is always hunting for new ways to get rich quick.
  • "There's an alms box at the temple that usually contains a few gold pieces. I hear Fazzir doesn't even lock it." (True)
  • "If you find yourself face to face with an owlbear, just play dead. It will quickly get bored and move on." (False)

Bank Features

The bank has the following features:

  • Service Counter. Sturdy hinges connect a wooden drop-down counter to the bank's window. At night, Quink folds up the counter and closes the window, then secures both with an iron grate.
  • Vault. A locked, reinforced door connects the bank teller's office to Quink's private quarters and a vault. Inside the vault are several strongboxes containing 250 GP worth of deposited wealth.

Bank Services

The bank offers the following services:

  • Take Out a Loan. A character can borrow up to 10 GP from the bank with an interest rate of 1 GP per day. There's no minimum payment due, but if the loan is left unpaid for long, word of the character's financial insolvency spreads throughout the keep.
  • Deposit and Withdraw Money. A character can deposit gold and other valuables at the bank. They can withdraw some or all the deposited savings during regular business hours at no cost.
A Hefty Bank Deposit

Quest: Bank Job

At the service counter, Quink asks the characters if they're adventurers looking for work. If they say yes, she leans in close and speaks to them in hushed tones. Read the following boxed text aloud:

"Yvette here is a lousy guard. There was a break-in recently on her watch, and the burglar got away. I fear the culprit might attempt another break-in, and I'd like you to prevent the heist—quietly. I can pay you a lump sum of twenty gold pieces for your services. What do you say?"

If the characters accept, Quink continues:

"I'd like you to stake out the bank tonight. If you see a burglar trying to enter, intervene and convince the criminal to leave at once. Remember, I'm paying for discretion. If you try to give the thief a trouncing, it will no doubt cause a scene. I want this matter resolved without violence."

Quink believes the culprit lives in the keep.

Thief in the Night

That night, a masked thief stealthily approaches the bank's door and attempts to pick its lock. The thief is Indifferent toward and wary of the characters if approached but doesn't immediately run away.

As an Influence action, a character can dissuade the thief and make one of these ability checks:

15 Charisma (Deception). The character tells the thief a lie, like saying the guards are coming.

15 Charisma (Persuasion). The character convinces the thief to pursue a different line of work.

15 Charisma (Intimidation). The character threatens the thief, who abandons the heist.

On a successful check, the thief lingers long enough for the characters to recognize Yvette, the bank's usual guard! On a failed check, she flees before they can get a good look at her.

Reward

Quink pays the characters 20 GP for stopping the heist as promised. If they also reveal the thief's identity, Quink is flabbergasted but adds a 10 GP bonus for the characters' exceptional work. Soon after, two guards arrive and arrest Yvette. After the arrest, Yvette no longer appears at this location.

title: 8: Traveler's Inn
html:
8: Traveler's Inn

This inn caters to weary travelers, merchants, and adventurers. It offers a range of accommodations depending on a customer's budget.

When the characters arrive at the inn, read the following boxed text aloud:

The smell of soap and lavender fills this warm inn. The front door opens to a lobby staffed by a stout dwarf behind a lacquered wooden counter with a shiny call bell.

"Greetings," the dwarf says in a deep voice. "Are you looking to book a bed for the night?"

The dwarf is Haldryck, the innkeeper.

Haldryck

Dwarf Innkeeper

  • Statblock:. Noble

Jovial and accommodating, Haldryck is a fast friend to anyone who visits his inn.

  • Epicurean. Good food and drink are the keys to Haldryck's heart.
  • Overseller. Haldryck advertises his inn's basic necessities—like clean sheets and doors with locks—as luxury amenities.
  • "The food at the tavern is the best in the Borderlands!" (Doubtful)
  • "My inn is the only place visitors to the keep can stay overnight." (False)

Inn Features

The inn has the following features:

  • Common Room. The common sleeping area is a large, open room with a handful of stiff cots and a crackling hearth. Patrons can also lay out their own sleeping mats on the floor for a safe—albeit uncomfortable—night's sleep.
  • Private Rooms. Customers with gold to spare can sleep in one of the inn's six private rooms. Each well-appointed room has four beds. Haldryck boasts that the beds in these rooms are bug free.
  • Wares. Haldryck rents and sells various bedding items, including wool blankets, woven sleeping mats, and pillows stuffed with goose down.

Inn Services

The inn offers the following services:

  • Rent a Cot. Cots in the common room are available to rent for 1 GP per night. Roll 1d4 for each character who rents a cot. On a 1, the character finds a dead bug on their pillow.
  • Rent a Room. A private room costs 5 GP per night. Roll 1d4 for each character who rents a room. On a 4, the character finds 1 GP under their mattress.
The Inn's Call Bell

Quest: Wake-up Call

After making introductions, Haldryck tells the characters they look light on their feet and in possession of good manners. He could use their help. Read the following boxed text aloud:

"Three guests sleeping in the common room this evening requested to be woken before sunrise, but I have a morning errand to attend to, so I won't be able to fulfill my promise to them. I'd like you to wake the early risers in my stead without stirring any of the other guests.

"In exchange, I can offer you a free night's stay in one of my private rooms. There's even one with a window! How does that sound?"

If the characters agree, Haldryck thanks them and describes the three guests who requested wake-up calls before returning to his duties.

Waking the Early Risers

When the characters arrive to wake the early risers, twelve people are asleep in the common room. The early risers are scattered about the room, dozing among other guests who don't wish to be disturbed.

To find and wake an early riser without disturbing the other guests, a character must succeed on a 12 Dexterity (Stealth) check. On a failed check, the character still wakes the early riser but bumps a grumpy sleeper in the process, rousing them from their slumber. The characters must make this check three times, one for each early riser.

Checking In with Haldryck

For waking the early risers, Haldryck rewards the party 5 GP, recommending they use it to rent a private room. If the characters completed the task without bothering any other guests, Haldryck gives the characters an additional 10 GP for their good work. Otherwise, he mutters about receiving a noise complaint from an unhappy guest.

Dwarf Innkeeper

  • Statblock:. Noble

Jovial and accommodating, Haldryck is a fast friend to anyone who visits his inn.

  • Epicurean. Good food and drink are the keys to Haldryck's heart.
  • Overseller. Haldryck advertises his inn's basic necessities—like clean sheets and doors with locks—as luxury amenities.
  • "The food at the tavern is the best in the Borderlands!" (Doubtful)
  • "My inn is the only place visitors to the keep can stay overnight." (False)

title: 9: Tavern
html:
9: Tavern

Dubbed the Drunken Dragon, this tavern caters to residents and visitors alike and hosts a nightly drinking game.

When the characters arrive at the tavern, read the following boxed text aloud:

The aroma of cooked mutton, fresh bread, and stiff ale wafts from this bustling tavern's doors. Inside, retired soldiers, chatty merchants, and weary travelers dot the taproom. A raised stage in one corner is empty.

A human man in an apron greets you from behind the bar. "Welcome to the Drunken Dragon. What can I getcha?" he asks in a smooth voice.

The man behind the bar is Umbrusk. After taking the characters' orders, Umbrusk invites them to play chug champion (see this location's quest).

Umbrusk

Human Barkeep

  • Statblock:. Commoner

Umbrusk serves up drinks, food, and gossip at the keep's tavern.

  • Eavesdropper. Umbrusk listens to his patrons' conversations.
  • Good Memory. Umbrusk never forgets a face or name.
  • "A traveler named Mallyn walks the trails outside the keep. If you meet her, say hello for me! She's my niece." (True)
  • "Whenever I order a cake, it gets seized by goblins, roadside bandits—you name it. I guess everybody likes dessert." (True)

Tavern Features

The tavern has the following features:

  • Taproom. The tavern's taproom holds a sticky bar counter, ten round tables, and forty chairs in varying states of disrepair.
  • Kitchen. In addition to hired cooks, Umbrusk's staff includes patrons who couldn't pay their tabs. They all work in a cramped, greasy kitchen behind a swinging door near the bar.
  • Stage. There's no formal vetting process for who can use the stage; the taproom's rowdy patrons loudly express their enthusiasm—or disdain—for anyone brave enough to perform.

Tavern Services

The tavern offers the following services:

  • Food and Drink. The tavern sells the items listed on the Drunken Dragon Handout. Give this handout to your players whenever they visit this location.

  • Buy the House a Round. For 20 GP, a character can buy a drink for everyone in the taproom. For the next 24 hours, that character has Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks made in the keep.
  • Solicit Rumors. Once per day, a character in the tavern can make a 10 Charisma (Persuasion) check to glean a rumor from the bartender or a chatty patron. 4Kalista, the keep's blacksmith, doesn't forge weapons anymore. (Partially true; she makes them only for the keep's militia.)

Quest: Chug Champion

The tavern's signature game is a nightly contest called chug champion.

Playing the Game

To play chug champion, participants—called "chuggers"—line up at the bar and pay 5 GP each to receive three pints of either heady ale or non-alcoholic cider (their choice). The goal is to drink the pints as quickly as possible over 3 rounds.

Each round, each participating character must succeed on a 12 Constitution saving throw to quaff the pint in one go. On a failed save, the character drinks too slowly and is eliminated along with a handful of other chuggers. Otherwise, they proceed to the next round. A character who succeeds on all three saves wins the game.

If multiple characters succeed on all three saving throws, compare the results of those chuggers' last saves, rerolling any ties. The character with the highest result places first, the character with the second-highest result places second, and any other characters place third.

A Tavern Stein

Winning the Game

The winner receives 25 GP. Second- and third-place chuggers win 15 GP and 10 GP, respectively.

title: 10: Guild House
html:
10: Guild House

This guild house offers membership to merchants and artisans, who enjoy benefits such as workshop space, library access, and armed escorts.

When the characters arrive at the guild house, read the following boxed text aloud:

Well-oiled oak beams crisscross the high ceilings of this stately guild house. Quiet murmurs and the sounds of crafting echo among workshops. A staircase ascends to a modest library.

A human woman in a wheelchair emerges from an adjacent office and politely greets you.

The greeter is the guildmaster, Toryn.

Toryn

Human Guild Master

  • Statblock:. Noble

This guild master helps fellow artisans get a good deal for their wares and services.

  • Judgmental. Toryn looks down on artisans who refuse to join the guild.
  • Witty. Toryn says smart things and always has the last word.
  • "Castellan Winvarle is the ultimate authority in the keep." (True)
  • "The Borderlands are home to all sorts of trades: musicians, mercenaries, treasure-seekers, spies—even monsters can have a profession. My advice? Pay them what they ask." (True)

Guild House Features

The guild house has the following features:

  • Administration. Toryn oversees the guild from a polished but cluttered oak desk in an office with a private elevator.
  • Library. The guild holds the largest collection of books and scrolls in the keep.
  • Workshops. Guild members ply their trades in 10-foot-square sections of a spacious room partitioned by hanging curtains.

Guild House Services

The guild house offers the following services:

  • Customize Equipment. A character can hire an artisan to customize their equipment, such as emblazoning a Shield with a symbol of their choice or embellishing the binding of a Spellbook. The standard rate is 5 GP per piece of equipment.
  • Research. The library contains books on history, magic, and the creatures of the Borderlands. For 1 GP, a character can spend 1 hour researching in the library. The next time that character takes the Study action relating to a subject covered by the library's books, they have Advantage on the Intelligence check made as part of that action. A character can benefit from this only once per day.

Quest: Chaos Unfurls

Once Toryn learns the characters are adventurers, she tries to hire them. Read the following aloud:

"I recently received a shipment of tempestuous magical scrolls. I need them stored in special scroll cases. If you tackle this chore for me, I'll pay you a total of twenty gold pieces. Be warned: the scrolls have a will of their own."

If the characters agree, Toryn leads them to a storeroom containing a pile of empty scroll cases and a warded chest that holds the scrolls. She instructs the characters to open the chest when they're ready, then wishes them good luck and departs hurriedly.

A Dangerous Magical Scroll

Ensorcelled Scrolls

When the characters open the chest, the scrolls erupt from it in a flurry of whirling parchment and shimmering ink. Roll Initiative.

Each round on Initiative Count 10 (losing Initiative ties), the scrolls fold themselves into weapons and deliver brutal paper cuts. Each character must succeed on a 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 Slashing damage. A character reduced to 0 Hit Points by a scroll has the Unconscious condition but is Stable.

There are two scrolls for every player character in the party. As an action, a character can try to stow a scroll in its case by succeeding on one of the following ability checks:

12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). The character deftly plucks a scroll from the air and puts it into a scroll case.

12 Intelligence (Arcana). The character pacifies a scroll with an arcane gesture, allowing it to be scooped up and peacefully stored.

12 Charisma (Intimidation). The character bullies a scroll, causing it to flee into a case.

Case Closed

If the characters encase all the scrolls, Toryn pays them 20 GP as promised. If the scrolls knock out all the characters, Toryn finishes the task before tending to the party. The characters wake up in her office with 1 Hit Point each. When the characters come to, Toryn apologizes sheepishly for putting them in so much danger, then awards them 10 GP for their effort.

title: 11: Temple
html:
11: Temple

The temple meets the spiritual needs of the keep. The curate, a human man named Fazzir, guides the temple's daily activities, which include conducting ceremonies, healing injured soldiers, and offering counsel in matters of ethics and morality.

When the characters arrive at the temple, read the following boxed text aloud:

The interior of this tall building has a lofty, majestic air. Rows of benches face an altar at the end of a spacious worship hall. Above the altar is an enormous stained-glass window of a sunrise.

Until recently, the temple's head priest was a human woman named Ivlis, but she recently departed the keep on a long-anticipated pilgrimage.

Fazzir

Human Priest

  • Statblock:. Curate

This spiritual leader offers counsel and healing to all who seek the temple.

  • Altruistic. Fazzir puts the needs of others before his own.
  • Trusting. Fazzir always assumes the best of people.
  • "The keep's former priest, Ivlis, left a large collection of books on all matter of subjects—even occult rituals." (True)
  • "Anyone entering the inner bailey is bound to cross paths with Shannik, sergeant of the guard. I think he's a little too hard on new recruits." (True)

DM Secret

Ivlis secretly leads the Cult of Chaos, an evil cult that feeds on destruction and disarray. Her supposed religious journey is a cover for her occult activities, which are detailed in the "Caves of Chaos".

Temple Features

The temple has the following features:

  • Alms Box. A stout pole near the temple's entrance holds a small box for visitors to leave donations. At any given time, the alms box contains 1d8 GP. The box is unlocked. A character who steals from the alms box must succeed on a 15 Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on D20 Test for the next 24 hours.
  • Sanctuary. This spiritual center can accommodate dozens of worshipers. Fazzir delivers sermons from the altar each dawn. His simple lessons appeal to a variety of religious traditions.
  • Underground Accommodations. Fazzir inhabits modest rooms in the temple's cellar. The cellar also contains two small spare rooms. Fazzir uses these rooms as infirmaries or guest quarters as circumstances demand.

Temple Services

The Sacred Services Handout lists available goods and services. Give this handout to the players whenever they visit this location. Fazzir provides the temple's healing and revival services as detailed on the Curate stat block.

Sacred Services
ServiceCost
Flask of Holy Water25 GP
Healing50 GP
Revival2,000 GP
Sacred Services Handout

May all who act with kindness and virtue Always stand upright.

May neither claw nor steel nor darkness hurt you; Be shielded by the light.

Quest: Priestly Duties

In Ivlis's absence, Fazzir is having trouble keeping up with the flood of new responsibilities. He asks the characters to help him with two clerical tasks.

A Holy Symbol

Impromptu Blessing

A married couple asked Fazzir to give them a blessing for safe travel for a romantic getaway. Fazzir needs two assistants to perform the ceremony.

To conduct the ceremony properly, two characters must each take the Study action and make a 10 Intelligence (Religion) check. On a successful check, the couple departs the temple with cheer. On a failed check, the couple postpones their trip, uneasy about what their journey might bring.

Occult Symbol

Last night, a vandal defaced the temple with a strange symbol. Fazzir doesn't recognize the symbol. He asks the party to scrub away the graffiti.

A blood-red bell is splattered onto the side of the temple in runny paint. A character who inspects the symbol and succeeds on a 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check recognizes the bell as the mark of the Cult of Chaos and an omen of future turmoil. If informed about the symbol's meaning, Fazzir finds the revelation deeply troubling. The mark washes off easily, but its stain on the priest's mind lingers.

Reward

After these tasks, Fazzir gives each character 3 GP regardless of their performance. He is just grateful for their support.

Good-Faith Discounts

It's unlikely that the characters will accumulate the gold required to revive a party member. At the DM's discretion, Fazzir might waive any of the fees on the Sacred Services Handout for those he believes show heroic potential.

title: 12: Inner Gatehouse
html:
12: Inner Gatehouse

This gatehouse houses on-duty soldiers and separates the civilian areas of the keep from the inner bailey (area 13).

When the characters arrive at the inner gatehouse, read the following boxed text aloud:

This gatehouse consists of a broad stone archway framed by a squat building constructed along the keep's inner wall. Battlements line its flat roof, atop which two guards stand watch.

The guards ask the characters about their business, then escort them to Andrella, Captain of the Guard.

Andrella

Human Captain of the Guard

  • Statblock:. Guard Captain

This captain is strong, stern, and just.

  • Perfect Posture. Andrella is as strict with her posture as she is with the law.
  • Role Model. Many of the keep's young people admire Andrella and enjoy her goodhearted mentorship.
  • "A dastardly bandit, Pral, accosts travelers along the trail. Apparently he's quite handsome; I'm sure he'll look even better behind bars." (True)
  • "The castellan tells me monsters are drawn to the Caves of Chaos in droves. I wonder why." (True)

Gatehouse Features

The gatehouse has the following features:

  • Garrison. Twenty-four soldiers, including Captain Andrella, are garrisoned in the gatehouse.
  • Gate. The gate features a massive oak double door. During invasions, soldiers can bar the doors with a heavy timber beam from the other side.
  • Murder Holes. Guards atop the gatehouse can thrust spears down at invaders through holes in the ceiling of the archway.

Gatehouse Services

The gatehouse offers the following service:

  • Requisition Uniforms. Characters who pledge to defend the keep can requisition uniforms from Andrella free of charge. Give those players one Borderlands Tabard each.
A Rack of Standard-Issue Spears

Quest: Testing the Defenses

Andrella has an unusual request. Once she learns the characters are adventurers, she dismisses the guards and says the following to the party:

"I want to observe how my soldiers would fare in an invasion scenario. As adventurers, you might be able to simulate such a threat.

"I'd like you to sneak past the guards stationed here after sunset and steal a pennant from the other side of the gate. As part of this exercise, you can't harm any on-duty soldiers, but I'll explain the situation if any of you are detained. "Are you up for the challenge?"

In exchange for their work, Andrella offers the characters a total of 25 GP.

Infiltrating the Guardhouse

During the night, eight soldiers stand watch outside the gatehouse: six on the roof and another two on the ground before the open gate. If necessary, use the Guard stat block to represent each soldier.

As an action, a character can try to bypass the soldiers and make one of these ability checks:

15 Dexterity (Stealth). The character slips past the soldiers undetected.

15 Strength (Athletics). The character scales the keep's sheer wall between regular patrols.

15 Charisma (Deception). The character fools the soldiers with a disguise or convincing lie.

On a successful check, the character bypasses the soldiers undetected. On a failed check, two soldiers spot the character and take them into custody, but other characters can continue the mission.

Debrief with Andrella

If at least one character reaches the pennant without getting caught, Andrella meets them afterward. She pays the party 25 GP as promised. If no characters were spotted, Andrella throws in an extra 15 GP and chastises the soldiers they evaded.

If all the characters are detained before anyone in the party can grab the pennant, Andrella visits the characters in a sparsely furnished detention cell and thanks them for testing her soldiers. She informs the soldiers about the training exercise and smugly pays the characters 25 GP on their release.

title: 13: Inner Bailey
html:
13: Inner Bailey

The sheltered inner bailey is where the keep's defenders live and practice combat drills.

When the characters arrive at the inner bailey, read the following boxed text aloud:

Targets and practice dummies dot this courtyard, which contains a large stable and poles with hanging rings. Cavalry soldiers train atop horseback while guards watch the area from the walls and towers that rise around it.

A mountain of a man in heavy armor tromps up to you. "No lollygagging!" he grouses.

The man is the keep's demanding and curmudgeonly sergeant of the guard, Shannik.

Shannik

Human Sergeant of the Guard

  • Statblock:. Guard Captain

Captain Andrella's second in command brooks no evildoers.

  • Brusque. When Shannik can substitute a reply with a grunt, he does so.
  • Shortsighted. Shannik's plans and actions fail to account for long-term repercussions.
  • "An adventurer is only as good as their gear. Oleira at the trader's shop is a friend of mine. She can sell you armor and weapons." (True)
  • "A real soldier can sleep off any injury. After a battle, I usually rent a bed at the inn. I always sleep better there." (True)

Inner Bailey Features

The inner bailey has the following features:

  • Cavalry Stable. The bailey contains a stable with thirty horses. These war-trained horses serve as mounts for the keep's cavalry.
  • Guard Towers. Four towers rise above the bailey, one in each corner. The smallest, to the southeast, holds up to eight guards. The southwest and northeast towers each hold one dozen guards, as well as food stores and other supplies. The Great Tower to the northwest is 60 feet tall.
  • Watches. Eight soldiers, two atop each tower, watch over the inner bailey at all hours. Use the Guard stat block for these soldiers if necessary.

Inner Bailey Services

The inner bailey offers the following service:

  • Weapon Upgrade. The keep ordered too many crossbows, which untrained recruits can't wield effectively. Shannik wants to trade the weapons for simpler ones. In exchange for 25 GP and a Shortbow, he can provide a character with a Hand Crossbow.

Quest: Shannik's Chores

Shannik hires the characters to complete a couple chores around the inner bailey. The characters can refuse his request, but Shannik asks with increasing insistence each time they visit the inner bailey.

Disrupting the Charge

Shannik wants to train two green recruits for the cavalry. He has them ride around the bailey for 10 minutes, spearing the hanging rings with lances.

During the exercise, Shannik asks the characters to disrupt the training by distracting the horses or their riders without causing injury to either. A character can do so by succeeding on one of the following ability checks. Consider these examples:

13 Wisdom (Animal Handling). The character guides a horse off course.

13 Charisma (Intimidation). The character tries to startle a horse or its rider.

A Cavalry Lance Laden with Training Rings

Catapult Installation

Shannik wants to install a catapult atop the Great Tower to defend against invaders. To do so, the characters must succeed on the following ability checks in this order:

15 Strength (Athletics). The character hauls supplies out of the stores in the southwest tower, across the bailey, and up the Great Tower.

13 Intelligence (Investigation). The character correctly assembles the catapult according to its blueprints.

13 Wisdom (Perception). The character calibrates the catapult by test-firing it at a target outside the keep's walls.

This task takes 1 hour. If at least one character succeeds on each check, the party completes the task. The characters can retry failed checks, but if they accumulate three failures, Shannik dismisses them, grumbling about their incompetence.

Reward

In exchange for completing a chore, Shannik pays a character 5 GP. A character can complete each of Shannik's chores only once. Thereafter, the sergeant greets the characters with a respectful nod whenever they visit this area.

14: Fortress
html:
14: Fortress

The castellan governs the keep from its fortress, a stone stronghold solidly built to withstand assault. Multiple towers rise above the main building, which is 30 feet tall. The fortress shelters emergency resources, municipal chambers, and the keep's armed forces. Militaristic banners and upholstered furniture decorate its dignified interior.

When the characters arrive at the keep fortress, read the following boxed text aloud:

Two round towers with pointed roofs flank this tiered stronghold. Archers march along its stone parapets, watching for signs of trouble. Two guards stand outside the fortress's iron doors; they acknowledge passersby with stern nods.

Fortress Features

The fortress has the following features:

  • Armory. Barding and lances for the keep's cavalry—thirty troops strong—are stored here, though the equipment is off-limits to the characters.
  • Barracks. Sparsely furnished quarters throughout the fortress can collectively accommodate up to thirty-six soldiers at once.
  • Great Hall. A spacious hall in the fortress hosts ceremonies, proclamations, and other receptions.
  • Private Chambers. Two lavishly decorated rooms are reserved for guests of the keep, while another belongs to the castellan.
  • Towers. Two peaked towers rise from the fortress.
  • Undercroft. Beneath the fortress are cellars containing vast provision stores, a cistern, and a dungeon with four stout cells for detainees and prisoners. If Yvette was arrested at the bank (see area 7), she is detained in one of the cells.

Fortress Services

The fortress offers the following services:

  • Defense. In times of crisis, the castellan can muster up to thirty-six trained soldiers from the fortress to defend the keep. The fortress also provides refuge during incursions.
  • Seat of Government. During the day, the castellan and his two assistants conduct business in the main building, where they hold audience with citizens and visitors of the keep.

Quest: Official Errands

Each official in the fortress spurs the characters to explore a different adventure setting.

Dwern the Scribe

The castellan's scribe, a dwarf man named Dwern, sits at a tidy desk in an austere office, documenting changes to the keep's inventory in a heavy ledger.

When the characters visit Dwern, he issues the following quest:

"I've commissioned a map of the wilderness beyond the keep. However, the map is sorely lacking in detail, and few are willing to brave the wilds to properly survey them—but you look like you're made of sterner stuff.

"If you help me finish my map by exploring the surrounding lands, I'll compensate you fairly."

If the characters explore three or more wilderness regions (see the "Wilderness" section) and report their findings to Dwern, the scribe pays them a handsome reward: a large, glittering gemstone (worth 100 GP), which they can sell to the jeweler for gold (see area 3).

Dwern

Dwarf Scribe

  • Statblock:. Noble

This gruff scribe prefers the company of books over people.

  • Bookworm. Dwern has read more books than anyone else in the keep.
  • Curmudgeonly. Dwern is ill-tempered toward younger people—which, to him, are most people.
  • "The guild house's library boasts a modest but impressive collection of books on history and magic." (True)
  • "There's an ancient statue somewhere in the forests north of the keep. It was once the site of strange rituals. Some say it still is." (True)

Elandra the Adviser

The castellan's trusted adviser, an elf woman named Elandra, operates in one of the towers. Carpets and tapestries decorate her chamber.

When the characters visit Elandra, she issues the following quest:

"While Castellan Winvarle protects the keep from outside threats, it's my duty to preserve the peace within its walls and ensure its citizens are content.

"I'd like you to visit a few businesses within the keep and help their owners with any odd jobs they might have. I recently acquired an item of arcane significance. Assist me in this effort, and the item is yours."

If the characters complete three quests within the keep and report back to Elandra, she rewards them with one magic item; roll once on the Magic Items table in appendix A (rerolling duplicates) to determine the item.

Elandra

Elf Adviser

  • Statblock:. Noble

Elandra provides guidance to the castellan and citizens of the keep.

  • Cautious. When presented with a choice, Elandra typically prefers the option with the least amount of risk.
  • Complainer. Nothing is ever good enough for Elandra.
  • "Every night, the tavern hosts a rowdy little drinking game with prizes. It's not for me." (True)
  • "Kalista, the keep's blacksmith, doesn't sell weapons to adventurers. If you want to know why, ask her." (True)

Winvarle

Human Castellan

  • Statblock:. Knight

The keep's noble commander leads his soldiers whenever the keep comes under attack.

  • Idealistic. Winvarle's ideals are rooted in lofty notions of righteousness.
  • Oblivious. While he excels at battle strategy, Winvarle scarcely knows the inner workings of his own keep.
  • "The Cult of Chaos is an affront to all that is good." (True)
  • "Anyone can pledge to defend the keep. Talk to Andrella in the inner gatehouse if you'd like to join the keep's defenders." (True)

Winvarle the Castellan

The keep's noble castellan, a human man named Winvarle, holds court daily in the great hall. A keen strategist, Winvarle casts his vigilant gaze toward the Caves of Chaos, where rumors of a sinister cult have surfaced (see the "Caves of Chaos").

When the characters visit Winvarle, he issues the following quest:

"Your arrival is fortuitous. I've heard whispers of a nefarious cult—the self-proclaimed Cult of Chaos—that reportedly operates in a cave network to the northeast. I believe the source of the cult's power resides in one of those caves.

"These lands yearn for heroes. For the good of the Borderlands and the people under my charge, I humbly ask you to investigate these rumors and, if need be, quash this evil before it reaches the keep."

Winvarle claims this quest is its own reward, but he adds that the Caves of Chaos abound with treasure, hoping to entice any characters who seek only to fill their coffers.

Castellan Winvarle also encourages the characters to meet with his adviser and scribe, who might have other tasks for them to complete.

Heroes' Return

Castellan Winvarle and the citizens of the keep celebrate the characters' heroic deeds

If the characters return to this location at level 3, having fulfilled all three keep officials' quests (detailed in the previous sections), they receive a heroes' welcome. That evening, Castellan Winvarle throws a celebration in the characters' honor and invites the citizens of the keep to participate in the festivities. At your discretion, any of the NPCs within the keep might be present at the celebration to mingle with the characters and show their appreciation.

At the height of the revelry, the castellan publicly thanks the characters and presents them a writ of congratulations. Give the players the Castellan's Letter Handout, which might inspire future adventures involving the Keep on the Borderlands.

Castellan's Letter Handout

Noble Adventurers,

I extend to you my deepest thanks. Your gallant efforts have forestalled the forces of chaos and made the Borderlands a safer place. Where there was once uncertainty, there is now hope.

Through your valiant deeds, you have proven yourselves to be more than mere mercenaries or vagabond explorers—you are heroes of the highest caliber. You have done an incredible service to the citizens of this keep, ensuring they can prosper in peace.

As a token of my appreciation, I have reserved a chamber in the fortress for you. You and your companions may come and go in the keep as you please. Henceforth, consider it a base from which you can embark on future adventures, no doubt for the betterment of these lands and the people who call them home.

Gratefully,

Winvarle

Castellan of the Keep

Ending the Adventure

Castellan Winvarle's celebration marks the end of this adventure, but there's still plenty to explore after that. The characters can continue to adventure in the Keep on the Borderlands, the Caves of Chaos, and the Wilderness (detailed in each respective section) until they've experienced all the Borderlands has to offer. You can also use them to tell stories of your own.

If you wish to advance these characters beyond level 3 and create new adventures for them, you need the core rules: the Player's Handbook, the Dungeon Master's Guide, and the Monster Manual.
